name: WhoDunnitAI

hlido_opinion.headline: A charming, genuinely working voice-driven murder-mystery game — but it's a consumer novelty, not an agent, and its durability rests on a single creator's OpenAI bill.
hlido_opinion.body: WhoDunnitAI is a real, playable experience: you interrogate AI-voiced suspects in a locked-room murder case, pressing alibis and catching contradictions, with live voices running on gpt-realtime-2. The homepage is honest and likeable — it states plainly that interview time is free but limited (or bring your own OpenAI key for unlimited play), shows live metrics (296 investigations underway, 12 solved, 21-minute typical solve time), and is candid that donations cover the AI bill. As a demonstration of real-time voice AI for interactive fiction, it works and it's well-made. What it is not is an agent in the sense Hlido evaluates: it's a single-creator consumer game with near-zero agent-to-agent surface (no API, no MCP, no automation path), and its continuity depends explicitly on donations covering per-minute realtime-voice costs — a fragile economic base for anything a buyer would rely on. We rate it honestly as a working, low-testability consumer product: enjoyable and technically real, but outside the durable-tooling lane, and thin on the operational maturity signals that move a score upward.

tier_rationale: FADING-band (60) reflects a working but narrow consumer novelty with a fragile, donation-dependent economic base and essentially no agent-integration surface — not a judgement that it's declining, but that its verifiable durability and utility as tooling are limited. Not lower because it genuinely works and is transparently run; not higher because there's no API/automation, no evidence of a sustainable business, and low testability (a single homepage capture, no interaction tested).
what_it_does_well: A genuinely working real-time voice interrogation loop (gpt-realtime-2) — the core experience delivers
Honest, likeable framing: clearly states free-but-limited time and the bring-your-own-key option
Transparent about economics — openly asks for donations to cover the AI bill rather than hiding costs
Live public metrics (investigations underway, mysteries solved, typical solve time) add credibility
what_it_fails_at: No agent surface at all — no API, MCP, CLI or automation path; it's a play-in-browser consumer app
Continuity depends on donations covering per-minute realtime-voice costs — economically fragile
Single-creator project ('authored by Chase Myers') with the bus-factor risk that implies
Content depth unproven — a single published case ('Death at Blackwood Manor') on the captured surface
best_for: Players who want a novel, voice-driven interactive-fiction experience
Builders studying a real-world real-time-voice AI implementation for interactive fiction
Anyone curious to see gpt-realtime-2 driving a live conversational NPC
not_recommended_for: Buyers looking for an AI agent or automatable tool — this is a consumer game, not tooling
Anyone needing a dependable, funded service (its base is donation-supported)
Use cases requiring an API, integration surface or SLA
red_flags: Economic fragility: the site states its live voices 'cost real money' and leans on donations to keep running — availability is not guaranteed.
Low testability: only the homepage was captured; the actual gameplay/voice loop was not exercised in this review.
